findings.statement: JAK-STAT pathway activity is raised in inflamed UC mucosa in all eight cohorts, the most direct link to an already drugged axis (JAK inhibitors). [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=8]

STAT3 transcription-factor activity (inferred from target genes, not its own mRNA) is up in all eight cohorts with the largest t values of the TFs checked, consistent with IL-6/IL-22/OSM-gp130 signalling. [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=8]

TNFa and NFkB pathway activity are up in all eight cohorts with very high t statistics, consistent with anti-TNF as the established drugged axis. EGFR, MAPK, PI3K, TGFb and Hypoxia are also up in all eight cohorts, but inflamed mucosa activates many pathways at once, so these broad signals are not specific.
AP1 is the top-ranked TF by cohort count (up in all eight cohorts, with the ATF/CEBPB family similarly up), a generic stress and inflammation signature rather than a specific target.

Negative result: p53 pathway activity is not raised; it is significantly lower in only a minority of cohorts, and the rest are non-significant, so no consistent p53 activation is seen. [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_down=3]

CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking (expression, replication in eight cohorts, genetics, literature and tractability), with several antagonists of CXCR1 and CXCR2 in clinical development (reparixin at late stage, navarixin and ladarixin at mid stage) but none established for UC. In single-cell data, its transcripts come almost entirely from neutrophils in the Gubatan dataset (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), while the Smillie dataset without neutrophils shows only sparse signal, so this is an infiltrating-cell signal rather than a tissue-cell change.

CXCL8 is up in all eight cohorts, and neutrophils make most of its inflamed-mucosa transcripts in the Gubatan dataset (share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]), whereas the Smillie dataset without neutrophils attributes it to macrophages and monocytes. Only two anti-IL-8 antibodies are at mid clinical stage.

Circuit: neutrophil-to-neutrophil CXCL8-CXCR2 autocrine/paracrine loop (sender Neutrophil CXCR4, receiver Neutrophil) is higher in inflamed than uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]). CXCL8 from neutrophils also reaches ACKR1 endothelial cells with the highest scores. This is co-expression, not proof of signalling, and ACKR1 is an atypical chemokine receptor.

Negative result: the neutrophil OSM to fibroblast (IL6ST) circuit has low scores and does not rise in inflamed mucosa for LP fibroblasts (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]); only a PADI4 neutrophil sender shows a new, low-scoring link. A neutrophil OSM to inflammatory-fibroblast axis is therefore not strongly supported by this ligand-receptor co-expression, and the returned list contained no OSMR pair.

IL1B is up in all eight cohorts and drugged (canakinumab approved for other indications). Its top circuit is monocyte-derived macrophage to neutrophil through IL1R2, a decoy receptor, so co-expression here does not imply activating signalling.

TREM1 is up in all eight cohorts and has only a phase 2 peptide (nangibotide), yet no ligand-receptor pair passed the expression thresholds, so no circuit can be assigned; it is a not-yet-targeted myeloid candidate.

DUOX2 is up in all eight cohorts with no drug in development, and CHI3L1 and AQP9 show the same profile of consistent upregulation without genetic support. They are biomarker-type signals more than validated targets.

caveats: Pathway and TF activities are inferred from bulk biopsy transcriptomes and mix epithelial change with immune infiltration; inflamed mucosa activates many pathways at once.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression, not proof of signalling; the Gubatan and Smillie datasets differ in whether neutrophils are captured, and dissociation enriches some fractions.
Neutrophil-derived signals (CXCR2, CXCL8) may reflect infiltration rather than a change of tissue cells.
TFs were checked only for the top-ranked set and STAT3; IL-23 and integrin axes were not queried directly in this pass.
